A1.justification: Both PDFs describe The Overcooked Generalisation Challenge. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganisation.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments, held-out-layout and FCP-partner evaluations, overfitting analyses and throughput measurements.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments including retained benchmark evaluations and additional Oracle, MEP-partner, cross-seed and error-analysis results.

M1.justification: The OvercookedUED generator/mutator, MAPPO pipeline and three network architectures are retained. Appendix A.5 preserves their components and parameter counts. Expanded placement and wall-budget descriptions do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: The five original layouts remain, but v2 substantially broadens evaluation conditions through MEP partner populations, cooperation between independently trained agents, and 24 mirrored/rotated circular layouts. These extend the partner populations and spatial test scenarios beyond v1's canonical-layout/FCP evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 adds Oracle policies trained jointly on all five evaluation layouts to the DCD and partner comparisons. The existing DCD algorithms and Random/Stay comparators remain, including in the appendix. v1's separately trained single-layout controls are not equivalent to these Oracles.

E3.justification: New protocols include joint-layout Oracle training for 200 million steps and 5,000 loops, self/cross-play matrices across three training seeds, and controlled symmetry evaluations. The principal DCD training budget and reward/solved-rate metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds Oracle capacity controls, training-versus-evaluation return curves, cross-seed cooperation analysis, symmetry tests and visitation heatmaps for successful and unsuccessful layouts. These substantially expand investigation of failure mechanisms beyond v1's overfitting and per-layout analyses.

E5.justification: Three DCD training seeds, eight population-training seeds, standard-deviation/standard-error reporting and the one-sided paired t-test are retained. Additional experiments extend these reporting practices without an established increase in repetitions or a new statistical testing procedure.

E6.justification: PAIRED and ACCEL results are revised: SoftMoE-LSTM PAIRED reward changes from 13.34 ± 5.70 in v1 Table 3 to 9.52 ± 1.02 in v2 Table 1; Table 12's solved rate changes from 14.62 ± 7.6% to 11.46 ± 2.1%. Oracle, MEP, cross-seed, diagnostic and additional throughput results are added. Some prose and plots retain older values.

T1.justification: The Dec-UPOMDP definition, joint reward/value formulation, environment policy and network mathematics remain equivalent. No substantive theorem, proof, assumption or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: Novelty wording changes: the conclusion specifies the first open-source cooperative multi-agent UED environment, narrowing v1's broader MARL claim, while the abstract drops the cooperative multi-agent qualifier. The central benchmark and joint layout/partner-generalisation contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets symmetry tests as evidence against spatial non-invariance, connects failures to difficult geometry and inadequate curricula, and notes that expert partners carry much of the cooperation performance. It also offers a qualified interpretation of cross-seed results. The original two limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents population CNNs, checkpoint selection at 10/50/100% achieved return, MEP entropy settings, additional budget accounting, teacher-placement details and explicit GPU requirements. Most architecture/hyperparameter tables, hardware information and repository/license disclosures already appear in v1.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused around cooperative versus competitive UED and open-source accessibility. v2 adds positioning against Neural MMO and JaxNav, plus citations concerning Genie and ad-hoc teamwork. The broad GPU-library survey and several other citations are removed; some single-agent discussion moves to Appendix A.3.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and benchmark narrative are extensively rewritten. v2 adds Research Challenges, reorganises evaluation/discussion and the appendices, makes Limitations standalone, and moves the impact statement out of the appendix.

P2.justification: The main paper and references adopt two-column formatting, with new or redrawn overview, design-space and architecture diagrams. Heatmaps and diagnostic plots are added, the existing-benchmark survey and throughput tables move to the appendix, and result tables gain Oracle and MEP blocks.

improvement.justification: Joint-layout Oracle controls, direct cross-seed tests and targeted diagnostics better distinguish generalisation failure from limited model capacity and expert-partner assistance. These gains are tempered by inconsistent updates: v2's text gives a 14.6 ± 7.7% solved rate versus 11.46 ± 2.1% in Table 12, and Figure 13 retains older FCP values despite Table 14's revisions. The added validation improves the paper, but these discrepancies limit confidence in exact comparisons.
